questions.q: What does the AND function require to return TRUE?
options: Every condition passed to it must be true
At least one condition must be true
Exactly one condition must be true, and no more
AND ignores all conditions after the first
questions.explain: AND returns TRUE only when all of its conditions are true — if even one fails, the whole AND returns FALSE.

questions.q: What is the risk of accidentally swapping AND for OR (or vice versa) in a formula?
options: The formula still calculates with no error, but silently returns the wrong answer for some rows
Excel throws an immediate #NAME? error
The workbook will fail to open
There is no risk — AND and OR always produce identical results
questions.explain: Mixing up AND and OR is a silent logic bug — the formula calculates fine but returns a wrong result for edge cases, since 'both must be true' and 'either is enough' are genuinely different conditions.

questions.q: What pattern from a nested IF chain does IFS specifically replace?
options: The same field tested against a new ordered threshold on every branch, without deep nesting
A single IF with only one condition
Any formula that uses SUMIFS
IFS replaces AND and OR entirely
questions.explain: IFS flattens exactly the pattern nested IF struggles with: one field checked against several ordered cutoffs, written as condition/result pairs with no nested parentheses.

questions.q: In `=IFS(Score>=90, "A", Score>=80, "B", Score>=70, "C", TRUE, "F")`, what is the purpose of the final `TRUE, "F"` pair?
options: It's the catch-all that runs only if every condition above it failed, equivalent to nested IF's final else
It forces Excel to always return "F" regardless of score
It is required syntax with no functional effect
It tells Excel to stop evaluating any further IFS formulas in the workbook
questions.explain: Since TRUE is always true, that pair is only reached once every earlier condition has failed — it's IFS's equivalent of nested IF's final fallback branch.

questions.q: What happens if an IFS formula has no catch-all pair and none of its conditions match?
options: IFS returns a #N/A error
IFS returns an empty string automatically
IFS returns 0 by default
IFS returns the first result listed, regardless of its condition
questions.explain: Without a TRUE catch-all (or some condition that's guaranteed to match), IFS returns #N/A when nothing matches — which is why including a deliberate catch-all pair matters.
